inferred_constraints.description: Mentoring relationships must be acyclic; there cannot be indirect cycles (e.g., if Alice mentors Bob, then Bob cannot mentor Alice, not even indirectly through a chain).

source_references.excerpt: And you cannot have loops either -- if Alice mentors Bob, then Bob cannot mentor Alice, not even indirectly through a chain. Mentoring always flows one way.

ambiguities.description: Project identification: The transcript states 'Projects have a project code, and each project also has exactly one project name.' While project code is clearly the identifier (and is used to reference projects in the business context), it is not explicitly stated that project code is UNIQUE across projects. Should we assume ProjectCode is a unique identifier, or could multiple projects share the same code?

ambiguities.description: Project name uniqueness: The transcript states each project has exactly one project name, but does not clarify whether project names are themselves unique or whether two different projects can have the same name. Is ProjectName a candidate identifier, or only an attribute?

ambiguities.description: Assignment cardinality on the Project side: The constraint states 'Every employee is assigned to at least one project, and never more than three at a time.' This bounds the Employee side (1–3 projects per employee) but does not specify cardinality on the Project side. Can one project have many employees, or is there also a limit? Must a project have at least one employee assigned?
